title: Invisible workload — myth flip: 'you're bad at delegating'
caption:
Myth: you're bad at delegating. Nope — you're doing the anticipating and monitoring nobody counts (Daminger, ASR 2019).
Which myth should we flip next? 👇

scenes.text: Nisha, 38, doesn't need a helper. She needs someone who *remembers* without being told.
phrases: "Asking is the part I'm tired of."

scenes.text: The work isn't the dishes. It's *remembering* the dishes, the dentist, the sports day.
phrases: Sociologists split this work in four:
Nisha carries the two that never clock out.

scenes.text: Women do 76.2% of the world's unpaid care work — about *4.5 hours* a day (ILO, 2018).

scenes.text: Own one job end to end — noticing it, planning it, doing it — instead of being handed it.
phrases: Pick one task and own the whole thing: noticing, planning, doing.
Read your 'remembering' list out loud at dinner once a week.
Then take a 12-minute walk — the WHO's 150 min/week adds up in bits.
